title: Surpassing thermal-state limit in thermometry via non-completely positive quantum encoding
summary: Conventional quantum thermometry assumes completely positive (CP) encoding maps, where the probe is initially uncorrelated with the environment. We consider realistic scenarios with initial probe-environment correlations leading to physically realizable non-completely positive (NCP) encoding, and show how such encodings can significantly impact temperature estimation of the environment.
